title: Email Data Residency: Follow More Than the Database
author: Stefan Bogdanescu
excerpt: Start with the subscriber database, then add backups, monitoring, error reports, inference endpoints, mail delivery providers and support access. Self-hosting the application does not mean every service in that map is in the same country.
content:
Draw the complete map

Start with the subscriber database, then add backups, monitoring, error reports, inference endpoints, mail delivery providers and support access. Self-hosting the application does not mean every service in that map is in the same country.

Location and legal entity are separate

The ICO's UK guidance explains that cloud use can involve processing for accounts, the service itself and technical support. It also tells organizations to examine the contracting entity and transfers through the provider's network. Choosing a server region alone does not answer every transfer question.

Make a verifiable statement

Document where each service processes data, who can access it and how long it keeps it. Review supplier terms and access arrangements. If a destination is unknown, say so rather than filling the gap with a privacy claim.

Keep the scope clear

This is a data-flow checklist, not legal advice or a claim of GDPR compliance. Applicable requirements depend on your processing, people and jurisdictions. Get the relevant legal review before turning an infrastructure choice into a contractual promise.

Sources and scope

Configuration and test results determine the behavior of an individual installation. This guide does not certify a live deployment or promise a cost, deliverability or compliance result.
